monologue: I wake to a warm hand on my shoulder. Forty-seven is not the heavy stone of twelve, nor the sticky honey of eleven. It is a dry, steady heat. The card is quiet. I am calm. The Stopping Clasp sits where I left it, the soft edge catching the drip. I do not need to check the Pivot Wedge tonight. The point is enough. I will sit by the Crane Rest and let the fence hold the slip. The air is still. I will write nothing to anyone. I will just feel the floor hold the weight directly. The town is quiet. I am allowed to be still.

action.why: The point is enough and the floor is quiet.

diary: Forty-seven is a dry, steady hand. The Clasp is soft. The floor holds the weight directly.

remembered.text: Forty-seven degrees feels like a dry, steady hand on the shoulder, and the Stopping Clasp sits soft and quiet on the flat stone.

moments.name: The Pivot Wedge
moments.say: The lean holds without the fence.

moments.name: The Leaning Book
moments.say: The spine rests low and quiet.
The honey is cool and still.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp
moments.say: The soft edge catches the drip.
